image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) floating on green rippled water. The duck on the left is in profile facing right, showing a glossy iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey body. The duck on the right is facing slightly left/forward, also displaying characteristic mallard plumage. Both are reflected in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both ducks clearly display the characteristic broad, flat, yellow-green bills typical of male mallards.
Dark eyes are visible on both subjects, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies appear streamlined and sit low in the water, indicating buoyancy and correct aquatic adaptation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit the specific breeding plumage of male mallards: iridescent green heads, distinct white neck rings, and grey/brown body patterning.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ducks are floating on water; their legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The folded wings on the sides of the bodies appear structurally sound, broad, and correctly positioned.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the right clearly shows the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers).

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples have a slightly repetitive, painterly texture that lacks the chaotic randomness of real water, though it is stylistically consistent.
The reflections are somewhat soft and lack the precise optical distortion expected from the specific ripple patterns, appearing slightly 'smudged' rather than optically refracted.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard) and rule out hybrid or generic 'duck' classifications.
To verify the structural integrity of the visible body parts and ensure no subtle fusion issues between the neck and body.
To audit the boundary between the duck's body and the water for any bleeding, melting, or incorrect contact shadows.
To assess the realism of the feather textures and check for AI-generated smoothing or noise artifacts.

Anatomical correctness of the head-neck-body transition
Consistency of lighting across both subjects
